paper.title: Improved Variance-Aware Confidence Sets for Linear Bandits and Linear Mixture MDP

settings.name_in_paper: Linear Bandits (with context sets A_k, unknown per-round variances)
unmapped: Noise is a martingale difference sequence with unknown, round-dependent conditional variance sigma_k^2 (not i.i.d.); rewards satisfy |r_k| <= 1
theta* in unit l2 ball; context sets A_k subset of unit l2 ball
settings.definition_quote: At each round $k = 1, \ldots, K,$ the algorithm is first given the context set $\gA_k \subseteq \sB_2^d(1),$ then the algorithm chooses an action $\vx_k \in \gA_k$ and receives the noisy reward $r_k = \vx_k \vtheta^* + \varepsilon_k,$ where $\vtheta^* \in \sB^d_2(1)$ ... We assume that $\abs{r_k} \le 1$ and that the noise $\varepsilon_k$ satisfies $\E[\varepsilon_k \mid \gF_k] = 0$ and $\E[\varepsilon_k^2 \mid \gF_k] = \sigma_k^2.$

settings.name_in_paper: Linear Mixture MDP (time-homogeneous, total reward bounded by 1)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic reinforcement learning (linear mixture MDP), not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Episodic MDP with horizon H, transition P = sum_i theta_i P_i with known base models, theta in l1 unit ball
Sum of rewards per episode bounded by 1; known reward function; time-homogeneous transitions
settings.definition_quote: A linear mixture MDP is an episodic MDP with the extra assumption that its transition model is an unknown linear combination of a known set of models. Specifically, there is an unknown parameter $\vtheta^* \in \sB^d_1(1)$, such that $P = \sum_{i = 1}^d \theta_i^* P_i$ where based models $P_1,\ldots,P_d$ are given.

conditions: theta* in unit l2 ball, actions in unit l2 ball

source.label: thm:oful
source.quote: The expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{algo:bandit} is bounded by $\E[\Reg^K] \le \widetilde{O}( d^{4.5} \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^K \sigma_k^2} + d^5)$.

results.notes: Paper's K (rounds) is T. Lambda_T = sum of unknown conditional variances sigma_k^2. Regret defined via theta* means against per-round best action in A_k. Algorithm is elimination over an epsilon-net; paper states it is not computationally efficient, recorded as exponential.

tuning: confidence parameter delta used in iota = 16 d ln(dK/delta)

source.label: lem:bandit-conf-sum
source.quote: With probability $1 - O(\delta \log K),$ we have $\sum_{k} \vx_k \vmu_k \le O\Bigg( d^{4.5} \big(\log^4 dK\big) \big(\log \frac{dK}{\delta}\big) \bigg( \sqrt d + \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^K \sigma_k^2}\bigg)\Bigg).$

results.notes: Lemma bounds sum_k x_k mu_k, which upper-bounds the regret on the event theta* in all confidence sets; failure probability is O(delta log K) rather than delta.

conditions: Assumption 2: sum of rewards in each episode <= 1 almost surely

source.label: thm:main_rl
source.quote: The expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} is bounded by $\E[\Reg^K ] \leq  \widetilde{O}\left(d^{4.5}\sqrt{ K }+d^9\right)$.

results.notes: Out-of-scope RL result. Õ hides polylog(H) factors. Regret is V*(s1)-V^{pi_k}(s1) summed over episodes.
